recorded.prompt:q-race-free:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-race-free:a: an independent reader (17-java-memory-model q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-race-free:a: ruled out: "if a program is correctly synchronized — it has no data races — then every execution of it appears sequentially consistent. Only programs with data races can observe the weaker, reordered behaviour." A data-race-free program's threads do not see writes reordered.
recorded.prompt:q-race-free:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-race-free:c: an independent reader (17-java-memory-model q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-race-free:c: ruled out: The stated guarantee is that the whole race-free program "appears sequentially consistent," not merely that volatile accesses fall in one total order (that narrower fact, from 5.1.2, applies to volatile accesses regardless of data races, and is a different guarantee).
recorded.prompt:q-two-monitors:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-two-monitors:a: an independent reader (17-java-memory-model q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-two-monitors:a: ruled out: Key Points #2: 'The happens-before edge from a monitor release is to any subsequent acquisition of the SAME monitor. Synchronizing on different objects provides no cross-thread guarantee.' Merely starting after the writer's block exited is not sufficient if a different monitor is locked; the same-monitor requirement, not temporal order alone, is what decides visibility.
recorded.prompt:q-two-monitors:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-two-monitors:c: an independent reader (17-java-memory-model q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-two-monitors:c: ruled out: Interview-specific Insights tricky question: 'Can synchronized guarantee ordering without any write in the synchronized block?' answered 'Yes — the lock itself establishes happens-before for all prior writes.' Visibility on lock covers ALL prior writes by that thread, not only the specific field the writer wrote, so reading 'the very field' is not the deciding condition.
